Lemma: H4376

ENGLISH GLOSSES TO TRANSLATE:
  Terse gloss: "To sell (goods, property, or persons); in Nifal, to be sold; in Hitpael, to sell oneself into servitude or evil."
  Readable gloss: "A thoroughly commercial verb that covers the full spectrum of ancient Near Eastern transactions — selling grain, land, daughters into marriage, and even persons into slavery. In its most theologically charged uses, God 'sells' Israel into the hand of enemies (Judg 2:14; Ps 44:12), treating military defeat as a divine commercial transaction. The Hitpael reflexive adds a striking moral dimension: kings who 'sold themselves' to do evil (1 Kgs 21:20, 25). French vendre and Spanish vender track the literal commerce, while German verkaufen and Arabic ba'a confirm the breadth from marketplace to metaphor."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: "Sell (Qal active)"
    Enriched: Active Qal selling: the straightforward transfer of goods, property, or persons for payment. Esau sells his birthright (Gen 25:33), Joseph's brothers sell him (Gen 37:27–28), and land transactions appear throughout Leviticus 25. Also includes the powerful theological metaphor where God 'sells' Israel to enemies (Judg 2:14; Ps 44:12). French vendre and Spanish vender consistently mark this active c...
    Existing Spanish translations: Y-los-vendió, me-vendisteis, venda, vende, vender, venderéis, vendieron, vendisteis, y-lo-venda, y-lo-vende, y-los-vendió, y-vendió
  Sense 2: "Be sold (Nifal passive)"
    Enriched: The Nifal passive: to be sold. Covers persons sold into slavery (Exod 22:3; Lev 25:39), land that cannot be sold permanently (Lev 25:23), and the rhetorical 'to whom were you sold?' of Isaiah 50:1. German verkauft werden and French être vendu capture this passive voice. The passive appears frequently in Levitical legislation regulating debt slavery and land tenure.
    Existing Spanish translations: Y-venderé, fue-vendido, fuimos-vendidos, fuisteis-vendidos, fuiéramos-vendidos, los-vendidos, se-vende, será-vendida, será-vendido, serán-vendidos, su-venderse, venderse, y-se-vende, y-será-vendido, y-serán-vendidos-, y-venderé
  Sense 3: "Seller (Qal participle substantival)"
    Enriched: The Qal participle used as a substantive noun: the seller, a vendor. Appears in legal and prophetic contexts contrasting buyer and seller (Isa 24:2; Ezek 7:12–13), and in Nehemiah's accounts of merchants trading on the Sabbath (Neh 13:16, 20). Spanish el que vende ('the one who sells') and French le vendeur mark this as a recognized social role.
    Existing Spanish translations: como-el-vendedor, el-que-vende, la-que-vende, vende, y-el-que-vende, y-sus-vendedores, y-vendedores-de, y-vendiendo
  Sense 4: "Sell oneself (Hitpael reflexive)"
    Enriched: The Hitpael reflexive: to sell oneself. Used literally of selling oneself into servitude (Lev 25:47; Deut 28:68 — 'you shall sell yourselves as slaves and no one will buy'), and figuratively of moral self-surrender: Ahab 'sold himself to do evil' (1 Kgs 21:20, 25). Spanish venderse and French se vendre capture this powerful reflexive force, where the subject is both seller and commodity.
    Existing Spanish translations: se-vendió, te-vendiste, y-os-venderéis, y-se-vendieron
